phase3_findings.description: After a successful emit_text every later final reply is hidden (only an INFO log); a later tool error or clarifying question written only in the final reply never reaches the user. agent.py is not in this PR's diff (behavior from #317), so pre-existing relative to this diff.

run_sql_display_line omits the row-cap fact on the headers-too-large branch and returns '' for a capped-but-uncut table; the agent relies on the pre-existing 'Result truncated at cap rows' note (AC11 scopes the display line to the display cut, so no AC is unmet).
Widget cancel message shown in a success-styled flashMeta.
No test that answer_prose_emitted is request-local under concurrent send_message calls (rating 5; file outside diff).
is_answer_marked strict 'is True' check has no negative test for truthy non-bool values (rating 5).
row_cap_marker_data stores int(cap) without validating it; builder and row_cap_of reader disagree on validity, so a bad cap vanishes silently.

components_to_blocks docstring (untouched) omits the new 'could not be displayed' text-block outcome.

checklist.claim: run_sql sets data=row_cap_marker_data(cap_size) on the DataFrameComponent only when row_cap_hit, and cap_size is the row cap in effect for that query (not a fixed 10000)
checklist.evidence: run_sql.py:84-85 reads row_cap_hit from df.attrs[TRUNCATED_ATTR] and cap_size from df.attrs[MAX_ROWS_ATTR]; line 147 sets data=row_cap_marker_data(cap_size) if row_cap_hit else {} on the DataFrameComponent. RowCapRunner.run_sql (safety/limits.py:84-103) computes cap = effective_row_cap(self._max_rows), the min of the constructor cap and the per-request effective max_rows (limits.py:36-52), and stamps max_rows=cap, or the inner runner's already-stamped max_rows, on the df. So cap_size is the cap in effect for that query, not a fixed 10000. markers.py:56-58 builds {row_cap: int(cap)}.

checklist.claim: DataFrameComponent accepts a `data` kwarg and keeps it as a dict attribute that row_cap_of reads, and existing producers never set the `row_cap` key for other purposes
checklist.evidence: RichComponent declares `data: Dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)` (core/rich_component.py:78). DataFrameComponent.__init__ forwards **kwargs to super (dataframe.py:48) and from_records merges extra kwargs into component_data (dataframe.py:~88), so `data=` is accepted and stored as a dict. row_cap_of (markers.py:61-73) reads getattr(rich,'data') dict and key 'row_cap'. The only producer of DataFrameComponent in src is run_sql.py:143-148, which passes data=row_cap_marker_data(cap) or {}; no other code sets a 'row_cap' key in data (grep of "row_cap" shows only markers, _table_payload, _format consumers and run_sql).

checklist.claim: row_cap_of returns None for bool, non-int, non-positive or non-dict data, and returns the int otherwise
checklist.evidence: markers.py:61-73 row_cap_of returns None if data is not a dict (67-69), None if cap is bool, not int, or <=0 (71-72), else returns cap. Tests at tests/unit/test_run_sql_display_line.py:144-154 cover this.

checklist.claim: _compute_table_payload adds row_cap to the payload before the size search, so the binary search keeps the payload, row_cap included, at or under _MAX_TABLE_PAYLOAD_BYTES
checklist.evidence: In src/sqllens/_table_payload.py, _compute_table_payload sets payload['row_cap'] at lines 180-182 when row_cap_of(rich) is not None. That is before the first _serialized_len check (line 184) and before the header-only check (192) and the binary search (196-209). Every measurement therefore includes row_cap. The search loop keeps the largest mid whose serialized length is <= _MAX_TABLE_PAYLOAD_BYTES, and lo=0 was already verified by the header-only check. So the returned payload, row_cap included, is at or under the cap.

checklist.claim: run_sql_display_line computes N from the same _compute_table_payload used by the formatter, so the agent's N equals the widget's row_count
checklist.evidence: run_sql_display_line (src/sqllens/_table_payload.py:227-260) calls _compute_table_payload(rich) (line 242) and reports payload['row_count'] as N (line 251). The formatter (src/sqllens/tools/_format.py:327 -> _build_table_payload at 829-836) calls the same _compute_table_payload(rich) on the DATAFRAME component and emits {'type':'table', **payload}, so the block row_count is the same value. run_sql.py:143-152 builds the DataFrameComponent and passes that same object to run_sql_display_line and into the UiComponent. _trim_blocks_to_budget only drops whole trailing blocks and does not rewrite row_count.

checklist.claim: The docstring claims the display line must never fail the query (it returns empty on any error)
checklist.source_excerpt: ``""``: the line is advisory and must never fail the query.
checklist.evidence: src/sqllens/_table_payload.py:236-260: the whole body of run_sql_display_line (is_introspection_query, _columns_and_rows, _compute_table_payload) sits inside try/except Exception, which logs logger.warning(exc_info=True) and returns "". This covers a RuntimeError, not just ParseError. The caller at src/sqllens/agent/tools/run_sql.py:150 uses the return value with no further handling, so an exception cannot escape and the query still succeeds. Only BaseException subclasses (KeyboardInterrupt, etc.) are not caught, which is outside the claim. I did not run the monkeypatch scenario, because test suites are not run.

checklist.claim: AC11: the new row_cap field is set only when the cap was hit, row_count+truncated equals the rows returned, and the block without 'type' serializes to at most _MAX_TABLE_PAYLOAD_BYTES
checklist.evidence: row_cap is set only when row_cap_of(rich) is not None (_table_payload.py:180-182); the marker is attached only when row_cap_hit (run_sql.py:147) and row_cap_of accepts only positive non-bool ints (markers.py:61-73).
